summary: Barrood Agency Inc. is a family-run independent agency founded in 1940 with offices in New Brunswick (46 Bayard St.) and Somerset (700 Easton Ave), writing personal lines, commercial lines, life/health, surety bonds and E&S placements, plus real estate, travel and notary services. LinkedIn lists it at 2-10 employees and a 4.3-star Google profile (22 reviews) with phone-based, form-based intake and no online booking or self-service quoting. All quote requests, policy changes, document requests and bond questions route to a small staff, so intake, document handling and follow-up are the likeliest places an agent would add leverage.

facts.fact: Founded in 1940; the agency says it serves clients' insurance, real estate and travel needs from offices in New Brunswick and Somerset.
Office addresses listed: 46 Bayard St. Suite 212, New Brunswick, NJ 08901 and 700 Easton Ave Floor 1, Somerset, NJ 08873.
The agency describes itself as 100% independent of any one carrier, representing several insurers in each market plus access to Excess and Surplus carriers.

Lines written include personal insurance, business coverage, life and health, a surety bond department (court, probate/fiduciary, license and permit, contract, fidelity bonds), plus real estate and travel divisions.

LinkedIn company page: 2-10 employees, headquarters Somerset, NJ, founded 1940, specialties Insurance, Real Estate, Travel, Notary Public; about text says 'over 80 years' serving thousands of clients through the New Brunswick and Somerset offices.

Google Business Profile (Barrood Agency Inc., 700 Easton Ave, Somerset): 4.3 stars from 22 reviews; phone (732) 247-8664; hours Monday-Thursday 9 AM-5 PM, Friday 9 AM-4 PM, closed Saturday and Sunday.

Service Center routes customers to a third-party billing/payment portal (erainsurance.epaypolicy.com), while policy changes and document requests are submitted by sending a request through the contact page.
A carrier contact directory lists Auto Owners, First Mutual, Foremost, Hagerty and MetLife with each carrier's payment phone number and payment website for customer self-service.
Bonding page offers an online application link for the New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor Bond (described as new for 2025) and tells visitors to call the office for rates or assistance.

The site's page sitemap shows roughly 20 trade-specific coverage landing pages (plumbers, electricians, HVAC, landscapers, painters, fleet, construction, cannabis, restaurant, church, etc.) with last-modified dates in February 2026, alongside a site-wide refresh dated March 2026.
The team page is an unfilled template placeholder showing 'Name', 'Title' and 'Bio To follow'.
Blog contains three posts, with the most recent dated November 2023.
Site includes an SMS opt-in/consent page and privacy language about text messaging consent, indicating the agency texts clients.

operations_signals: Two physical offices (New Brunswick suite and Somerset first-floor office), consistent with a split book of Middlesex and Somerset county business (https://www.barrood.com/contact/)

Business hours are staffed-office hours only - Mon-Thu 9-5, Fri 9-4, closed weekends - with no published after-hours or 24/7 claim line (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)

Main tracked phone number is (732) 247-8664 on the Google profile; the agency's own pages present quote, change and document requests as web-form submissions rather than phone or calendar booking (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)

Intake is a 'Start Your Quotes' web form with separate personal and commercial quote request paths; no instant rating, live chat or online scheduling was present on the fetched pages (https://www.barrood.com/quotes/)

Policy changes and document requests (ID cards, certificates of insurance) are submitted via a request form on the contact page, i.e. a human has to process each one (https://www.barrood.com/service-center/)
Billing and payments are pushed to a third-party portal and to each carrier's own payment site, meaning staff reconcile across many carrier systems (https://www.barrood.com/service-center/)
Claims are carrier-direct; the agency publishes a carrier-by-carrier directory of payment phone numbers and websites rather than a single claims intake (https://www.barrood.com/billing-claims/)
Surety bond intake is partly self-service (online application for the NJ Home Improvement Contractor Bond) but rates and issuance still require calling the office (https://www.barrood.com/bonding/)
Service area is described as Central New Jersey, served from the two offices (https://www.linkedin.com/company/barrood-agency)
hiring_signals: No hiring signals found: the site has no careers page (https://www.barrood.com/careers returns 404) and the company's LinkedIn page showed no current job listings in guest view (https://www.linkedin.com/company/barrood-agency/jobs/)
LinkedIn lists only 4 people associated with the company and a 2-10 employee size band, suggesting little or no recruiting volume to observe (https://www.linkedin.com/company/barrood-agency)
review_themes: Recurring praise for individual agents being quick to respond to calls and emails, with one reviewer crediting a named account manager for staying a loyal customer (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)

Google's review filter shows an 'easy to work with' theme appearing twice, and multiple reviews cite getting better rates or 'best rates' (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)

At least one strongly negative review on the same profile ('my experience has been horrible'), so service consistency is not uniform (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)

Only 22 reviews total, and the visible reviews are 6-12 years old, so review recency is weak relative to 80+ years in business (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)
Praise centers on named individuals rather than the agency as a whole, indicating service quality is person-dependent (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)
tech_footprint: WordPress site on a shared agency-network platform (uploads path /wp-content/uploads/sites/229/, 'advisorevolved' and era-division asset filenames), i.e. a template website supplied by a larger agency network rather than a bespoke build (https://www.barrood.com/reviews/)
Quote and contact forms are Gravity Forms on WordPress; no embedded rating engine or online booking found on the fetched pages (https://www.barrood.com/quotes/)
Surety bond applications run through an e-surety.net portal link (asc.e-surety.net) for the NJ Home Improvement Contractor Bond (https://www.barrood.com/bonding/)
Premium payments route to a third-party epaypolicy.com portal plus individual carrier portals (https://www.barrood.com/service-center/)
Google Business Profile is claimed and the site has a dedicated review-request page linking to the Google review form via place ID (https://www.barrood.com/reviews/)
SMS/text-messaging consent page and policy indicate use of text messaging with clients (https://www.barrood.com/sms-consent/)
Content footprint is thin: 3 blog posts ending November 2023, an unfilled team page, and a bond guidelines PDF still hosted on a legacy Wix storage URL (https://www.barrood.com/team/)
Site publishes no self-service client portal of its own; 'Client Services' is a hub page of links to external portals (https://www.barrood.com/service-center/)
growth_signals: Site was rebuilt/expanded in 2026: roughly 20 trade-specific coverage landing pages dated February 2026 and site-wide page updates through March 2026, indicating investment in commercial-lines marketing (https://www.barrood.com/page-sitemap1.xml)
Two offices and 80+ years in business since 1940, with real estate, travel and notary services alongside insurance (https://www.linkedin.com/company/barrood-agency)
Added a 2025 product line around the New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor Bond, targeting contractors (https://www.barrood.com/bonding/)

Current site metadata frames the agency as an independent agency located in Somerset, NJ, while the record address is New Brunswick - consistent with a Somerset office becoming the operational center (https://www.barrood.com/contact/)

Google profile has only 22 reviews despite eight decades of operation, suggesting limited review-generation effort rather than low customer volume (https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7_9M4lDGw4kRxw1DJzCTAtk)
decision_maker: Unknown. No owner or GM is named on the agency's own site (its team page is an unfilled 'Name / Title / Bio To follow' template). The company's LinkedIn page lists David Barrood among 4 employees with no title shown, and Google reviews refer to a 'David' as their agent - title unconfirmed from public sources.

inferences.inference: Every inbound request - quote, policy change, ID card, certificate of insurance, bond rate question - is handled by staff manually.
inferences.reasoning: The service center sends changes and document requests through a contact form, quotes go through a form with no instant rating, and the bonding page says to call for rates; no self-service client portal exists on the site.

inferences.inference: A 2-10 person staff covering personal lines, commercial lines, life/health, bonds and E&S placements plus real estate, travel and notary work means role-switching and fragmented triage.
inferences.reasoning: LinkedIn gives a 2-10 employee band and 4 associated people, while the sitemap shows 80+ distinct coverage pages spanning five product families.

inferences.inference: Response speed depends on individual agents and is the agency's main reputation risk as volume grows.
inferences.reasoning: Reviews praise specific named agents for replying fast and include one 'horrible experience' review; with only 22 reviews and no visible intake automation, staffing is the bottleneck.

inferences.inference: Carrier-heavy back office creates recurring manual reconciliation and status-chasing work.
inferences.reasoning: The billing page lists at least five carriers with separate payment phone numbers and portals, and billing is routed to a third-party epaypolicy portal rather than managed in one system.

inferences.inference: Demand is likely seasonal and event-driven, straining a small team.
inferences.reasoning: Medicare-related pages (AEP-driven), contractor bond demand tied to the new 2025 NJ home improvement bond, and real estate/travel closings all cluster in specific windows; this is an inference from the product mix, not a stated claim.

inferences.inference: The agency is investing in commercial-lines growth but has little internal marketing capacity.
inferences.reasoning: About 20 trade-specific landing pages were published in February 2026, yet the blog stopped in 2023 and the team page remains a placeholder - template content was deployed without staff follow-through.

inferences.inference: Real estate, travel and notary lines may be legacy or low-volume rather than active growth areas.
inferences.reasoning: They are listed on LinkedIn and the homepage, but the sitemap shows no dedicated real estate, travel or notary pages among the 2026 build-out.

data_gaps: No hiring or job-posting data: no careers page (404), Indeed returned a bot-verification wall, and LinkedIn guest view showed no postings.
Review coverage is thin: only 22 Google reviews and a limited guest view of 3-4 review texts; Yelp and Facebook blocked access (403 / login wall), and no BBB profile could be reached without search.

Web search providers were rate-limited or blocked during this run (Exa/OpenAI exhausted, Brave/Gemini unconfigured, DuckDuckGo/Google/Bing/Mojeek blocked or returning junk), so local news, awards and directory listings could not be checked.
No published agency phone, email or hours on the agency's own pages - tracked phone (732) 247-8664 and hours come from the Google Business Profile only.
No named owner, principal or GM with title found on the agency's site or LinkedIn; the team page is a placeholder.
No verified revenue, premium volume, policy count or carrier appointment list; only the handful of carriers listed on the billing page were observable.
After-hours and emergency-claim coverage is unstated; claims are referred to carriers, but no 24/7 agency line is documented.
Whether the New Brunswick office is staffed for walk-ins (versus mail/records only) could not be confirmed; the site metadata and LinkedIn headquarters both point to Somerset.
